rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose noun for movement or a measured quantity going downward.

example.jyutping: go3 hei3 kau4 maan6 maan6 haa6 gong3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken choice for physically falling and for a level, price, or rating going down.

example.english: I fall whenever I walk too fast.
example.jyutping: ngo5 haang4 faai3 di1 zau6 wui5 daat3 can1

rows.note: Use this for something coming down from above, especially rain or an object descending through the air.

example.english: Heavy rain can fall from the sky, and the mountain road soon floods.
example.traditional: 大雨由天上落下，山路好快就積水。
example.jyutping: daai6 jyu5 jau4 tin1 soeng6 lok6 haa6 saan1 lou6 hou2 faai3 zau6 zik1 seoi2

rows.note: Use this specifically for a waterfall, not for an ordinary downward movement.

example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 heoi3 tai2 buk6 bou3 laa1

rows.note: Use this for a decline in greatness, power, or social status.

example.english: This family has suffered a fall from grace.
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 gaa1 zuk6 ji5 ging1 seoi1 lok6 laa3

rows.note: Use this when “fall” means becoming bad or entering a negative condition.

example.english: Things slowly fall into a bad state.
example.jyutping: gin6 si6 maan6 maan6 bin3 waai6 zo2

rows.note: Use this colloquial verb when a structure, organization, or undertaking collapses or goes under.

example.english: That company could fall apart at any time.
example.jyutping: gaan1 gung1 si1 ceoi4 si4 wui5 lam6
